chunks: From him, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Patience is two types: patience upon affliction is good and beautiful; and the superior of the two types of patience is abstinence from the prohibitions.

key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Abstinence, piety, God-consciousness in avoiding sins

ai.seo_question: What is the superior form of patience in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elevates 'war'' (piety/self-restraint) above passive endurance, framing it as the active, superior discipline of avoiding divine prohibitions. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on proactive moral vigilance rather than mere stoicism, aligning with the concept of 'sabr al-jalil' (the great patience) required to maintain spiritual integrity amidst worldly trials. The narration underscores that true patience is not just bearing suffering, but actively restraining the self from sin, a core tenet of ethical conduct in Shia jurisprudence and spirituality.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The patience is two (types of) patience – Patience upon the affliction is good, beautiful; and (even) superior of the two (types of) patience is the abstinence from the Prohibitions’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from his father from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has narrated it in a marfu’ manner from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘
Patience is of two kinds: to exercise patience in hardship, which is good and graceful, yet, the best of patience is that which is exercised to stop one from committing what Allah has prohibited.”’
